data.content_ref: inline:SRC_003's claimed causal mechanism is that common-cause traffic shocks exhaust small services' recovery resources while a large service's redundant pools absorb them, but this conflates a single correlated cause (common-cause traffic) with the full joint failure distribution. The problem asks whether a decentralized network is more resilient to correlated failure overall, not whether it is more resilient to one specific correlated failure mode. SRC_003 restricts its mechanism to traffic-spike/cascading-load scenarios (its counterconditions even concede resilience if shocks are truly independent), so it does not establish the general claim that the network is 'often less resilient to correlated failure' — it only identifies one causal channel. A traffic-spike channel is a candidate mechanism, not a demonstrated general one.
